name: Intikhab Khursheed
heroRoles: Full-Stack & AI Engineer | Independent RTL Verification Researcher
summary: I build production software for healthcare, SaaS, and business workflows, and explore how verification methods improve system reliability.
statusText: Available for full-time, remote, and contract software roles | Open to thesis-based MSc research opportunities
about:
I am a Full-Stack and AI Engineer with 3+ years of professional experience building applications for healthcare, SaaS, and enterprise workflows. My core stack includes React, Angular, Node.js, TypeScript, Python, MongoDB, Docker, Socket.io, JWT/RBAC, and AI APIs.

I built an offline-first Hospital Management System deployed at DHQ Bajaur Government Hospital in Pakistan. The system supports 500+ daily users and gave me practical experience building software for real operational workflows.

Alongside software engineering, I have developed an independent interest in RTL verification and formal methods. In an independent RTL research assignment guided by Dr. Umang Mathur at NUS School of Computing, I implemented a SystemVerilog vector dot-product accelerator, wrote SystemVerilog Assertions, reimplemented the design in Anvil HDL, and studied five documented RTL bugs from OpenTitan, iDMA, common_cells, and CVFPU.

I am applying for thesis-based MSc opportunities while remaining open to full-stack, AI engineering, verification-tooling, and software-engineering roles.
contactIntro: Available for full-stack, AI engineering, SaaS, and verification-tooling opportunities. Also open to thesis-based MSc research conversations in dependable systems, AI, software engineering, cybersecurity, formal methods, and RTL verification.

projects.title: Anvil RTL Bug Study — Hardware Verification & Timing Safety
projects.subtitle: Independent RTL Verification and Timing-Safety Study
projects.description: Real SystemVerilog bugs can survive simulation and review when back-pressure, parameterization, or functional completeness are not fully verified.
projects.problem: Real SystemVerilog bugs can survive simulation and review when back-pressure, parameterization, or functional completeness are not fully verified.
projects.role: Analyzed five documented bugs from OpenTitan, iDMA, common_cells, and CVFPU; built three standalone SystemVerilog/Verilator reproducers and SVA properties.
projects.result: Identified that Anvil can prevent specific channel-level back-pressure mechanisms, partially reduce risk in FIFO bookkeeping when sequencing is expressed through channels, and does not replace width checking or functional verification.

projects.title: Anvil Vector Dot-Product Accelerator
projects.subtitle: SystemVerilog, SVA, and Anvil HDL Comparison
projects.description: Explore the boundary between timing-safe HDL guarantees and functional RTL verification.
projects.problem: Explore the boundary between timing-safe HDL guarantees and functional RTL verification.
projects.role: Implemented a 4-lane vector dot-product accelerator in SystemVerilog with IDLE/LOAD/REDUCE/OUTPUT FSM, ready/valid back-pressure, partial-lane support, and six SVA properties; reimplemented it in Anvil HDL.
projects.result: Differential testing across seven cases matched expected results and showed that timing safety does not automatically establish functional correctness.
